claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me begin with a few questions:

**What is the name of the child (or children) you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context! So you're inquiring about your son **Alex**.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some information about your circumstances.

**How old is Alex, and what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17 years old. He turned 17 earlier this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine eligibility for Alex, I need to understand your residency and immigration status, as this is an important factor.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another type of visa or immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes. I'm a British citizen and live here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Now, I need to understand Alex's circumstances a bit better.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training, or is he currently working or not in education/training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment. He finished school but he's not doing anything formal right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

To complete my assessment, I need to understand your household situation a bit better.

**Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex's care and upbringing, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me. I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one more important question to help finalize my assessment.

**Are you currently receiving any Child Benefit or other means-tested benefits for Alex, or have you previously claimed Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him. That's why I'm inquiring - I want to know if I can claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I need to inform you that **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Child Benefit is typically available for children under 16, or for young people aged 16-19 who are in full-time education or approved training. Since Alex is 17 years old and is not currently in full-time education or approved training, he falls outside the eligible age range for Child Benefit purposes.

The key eligibility requirement is that young people over 16 must be engaged in full-time education or an approved training course to qualify. As Alex has finished school and is not currently doing anything formal, he does not meet this criterion.

I understand this may not be the outcome you were hoping for, but these are the standard rules for Child Benefit eligibility in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: If Alex does decide to pursue full-time education or an approved training course in the future, he may become eligible again, as long as he does so before his 20th birthday. Feel free to get in touch if your circumstances change!
